job.style: a passage that starts from a common wrong idea and corrects it

passage: Many people believe that muscles grow larger while you are lifting weights at the gym, but this is a common misunderstanding. In reality, exercise creates tiny tears in your muscle fibers, and the actual growth and repair process happens during your rest days, not during the workout itself. To support this growth, your body needs a balanced diet, but simply consuming excess protein powder without proper training will not magically build muscle. Another myth is that you must use expensive gym machines to build strength. You can effectively strengthen your muscles using your own body weight through exercises like push-ups or squats. Furthermore, some people think that if they stop exercising, their muscle tissue will transform into fat. This is biologically impossible; muscle and fat are two completely different types of tissue. If you stop being active, your muscles may shrink from lack of use, and you might gain fat if you continue to eat the same amount of calories, but one does not turn into the other. Finally, remember that sweating is just your body’s way of cooling down, not a direct measurement of how much fat you have burned. Consistent, balanced activity is the key to a healthy body.

items.evidence: In reality, exercise creates tiny tears in your muscle fibers, and the actual growth and repair process happens during your rest days, not during the workout itself.
items.q: Meena lifts weights on Monday and does not exercise on Tuesday. When do her muscles actually grow bigger?
options: During Tuesday, while the tiny muscle tears are repaired
During Monday, while she is lifting the heavy weights
During Tuesday, only if she lifts weights again
During Tuesday, only if she drinks extra protein powder
items.explain: Exercise makes tiny tears in muscle fibres, and growth and repair happen on rest days, not during the workout.

wrong.why: thinks muscles grow during the lifting itself
thinks training every day is needed and rest days are bad
thinks extra protein is what makes muscles grow

items.evidence: To support this growth, your body needs a balanced diet, but simply consuming excess protein powder without proper training will not magically build muscle.
items.q: Kabir drinks lots of protein powder every day but never exercises. What will happen to his muscles?
options: They will not grow, as training is also needed
They will grow big, as protein builds muscle alone
They will turn into fat, as he does not exercise
They will grow, if he also eats a balanced diet
items.explain: Extra protein powder without proper training will not build muscle. Diet only supports the growth that training starts.

wrong.why: thinks extra protein alone makes muscles big
thinks unused muscle turns into fat
picks the nearby detail about a balanced diet and ignores the need for training

items.evidence: You can effectively strengthen your muscles using your own body weight through exercises like push-ups or squats.
items.q: Sana says nobody can build strength without gym machines. Which plan would prove her wrong?
options: Doing squats with no weights except her body
Lifting heavy weights on gym machines daily
Drinking protein powder instead of training
Sweating a lot to burn away body fat
items.explain: Push-ups and squats use your own body weight and still make muscles stronger, so no machines are needed.

wrong.why: believes strength exercise needs machines or heavy weights
mixes up sweating and fat loss with building strength

items.evidence: If you stop being active, your muscles may shrink from lack of use, and you might gain fat if you continue to eat the same amount of calories, but one does not turn into the other.
items.q: Ajay stops playing football but keeps eating the same amount of food. What most likely happens to his body?
options: His muscles get smaller and he may add some fat
His muscles slowly change into fat over time
His muscles keep growing from his past training
His muscles stay the same, as rest builds muscle
items.explain: Unused muscles shrink, and eating the same calories can add fat, but muscle never turns into fat.

wrong.why: thinks past training keeps working without activity
over-generalises the idea that growth happens on rest days

items.evidence: Finally, remember that sweating is just your body’s way of cooling down, not a direct measurement of how much fat you have burned.
items.q: Rahul sweats much more than Dev during the same run. What does this tell us?
options: Rahul's body is cooling itself more than Dev's
Rahul has burned more fat than Dev today
Rahul's muscles are growing bigger than Dev's now
Rahul has more fat stored in his body than Dev
items.explain: Sweating is only the body's way of cooling down. It does not show how much fat was burned.

wrong.why: believes the myth that sweat measures fat burned
thinks muscles grow during the exercise itself
thinks more sweat means more body fat
